cs.t: This really depends on what you're replacing.  Replacing a standard electric water heater that uses ~$500/year of electricity with a heat pump water heater that uses ~$100/year (that's about what ours uses) has a pretty quick payback period.

My mom had a Heat Pump water heater at her house and I was always having to go and fix it or clean the filter. It would start beeping loudly in the middle of the night when it wanted attention.  The hot water was frequently not very hot. Hopefully the new heat pump water heaters are better.  The advantage of resistance heating is simplicity and cost, with no moving parts. Solar panels are so cheap now they make it hard to justify the expense of the heat pump, assuming you have room to mount the panels.
